newsitem.title: USA: HP to announce Internet strategy next month.
newsitem.headline: HP to announce Internet strategy next month.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co plans to announce a broad Internet strategy early next month, the company's chief executive officer told Reuters on Monday.

"Stand by in early December," CEO and President Lewis Platt said after a press conference here on the company's new encryption strategy. "We're going to be making quite a set of announcements about our whole Internet strategy and the kind of products we'll be coming out with."
Although the surging growth of the Internet has greatly boosted HP's sales, the company has not been closely identified with the global computer network in the past.
Next month's announcement is intended to raise the company's profile in the Internet marketplace, Platt said.

"The Internet is something that has not escaped us," he said. "I don't think we've taken quite as vocal a lead in that area or quite as obvious a position as some of our competitors have, but it's a really important market to us."

Last week the company unveiled a series of new products aimed at businesses building public web sites and "intranets," private computer networks built with the same technologies as those used on the Internet.
At Monday's briefing, given jointly with Microsoft Corp and Intel Corp, HP edged into another critical Internet niche, encryption technology.

"This is a more visible sign of our commitment to the Internet space," Platt said of the encryption initiative, called the International Cryptography Framework. "The Internet probably has about as much to do with driving our business today as any other development in the world."
Encryption, which scrambles computer data so it cannot be read without a password or software "key," is an essential component of global communications and online commerce.

U.S. law prohibits the export of products with the latest, most powerful encryption features. On November 15 President Clinton signed an executive order liberalizing but not removing the export limits.

Hewlett-Packard's framework effectively allows encryption features in a product to be turned off if the product is destined for sale abroad. The encryption features can be restored later -- if export rules change, for instance.
The U.S. government has already approved the framework for export, company officials said.
